question: How do I register for classes at HANU?
answer: Log into the HANU Student Portal, go to "Course Registration", pick your intended session, and add classes before the add/drop deadline listed on the academic calendar.

question: What is the add/drop deadline for Fall 2026?
answer: The add/drop deadline for Fall 2026 is the end of the second week of the semester. After that date, dropping a course records a "W" (withdrawal) on the transcript.

question: Can I register for a course if I have not completed the prerequisite?
answer: No. The registration system blocks enrollment in courses whose prerequisite has not been passed. You may request a prerequisite override from the department chair if you have equivalent experience.

question: How many credits can I register for as a first-year student?
answer: First-year students may register for up to 18 credits per semester without an advisor override; students on academic probation are capped at 12 credits.

question: What happens if the course section I want is full?
answer: Join the waitlist through the Student Portal. You will be automatically enrolled if a seat opens, and you will receive a notification within 24 hours of the seat becoming available.

question: How do I switch from one course section to another?
answer: Use the "Swap Section" option in the registration portal before the add/drop deadline; after that date you need instructor and advisor approval.

question: Can I audit a course instead of taking it for credit?
answer: Yes. Select "Audit" instead of "Credit" during registration. Audited courses do not count toward your degree credit total and appear on the transcript with a grade of "AU".

question: How do I request an override for a closed course?
answer: Message the course instructor through the portal requesting an override code, then enter the code on the registration page before the add/drop deadline.

question: What is a registration hold and how do I clear it?
answer: A hold blocks registration until an issue (unpaid balance, missing immunization record, advising sign-off) is resolved. Check the "Holds" tab on your Student Portal dashboard for the reason and the office to contact.

question: When does registration open for returning students?
answer: Registration windows open by credit-hours earned, roughly four weeks before the semester starts; seniors register first, followed by juniors, sophomores, and first-year students.

question: Can I take a class in another department if I am not majoring in it?
answer: Yes, as long as you meet the course prerequisites and there is available capacity; some departments reserve a fixed number of seats for majors during the first registration window.

question: How do I withdraw from a single course after the semester has started?
answer: Submit a withdrawal request through the Student Portal before the withdrawal deadline; the course will show a "W" grade instead of a letter grade.

question: When are final exams scheduled?
answer: Final exams are held during exam week, the week following the last day of regular classes each semester; the exact schedule is posted on the Registrar's exam calendar page.

question: What do I do if two of my final exams are scheduled at the same time?
answer: Report the conflict to the Registrar's Office at least two weeks before exam week; they will reschedule one exam through the conflict exam process.

question: Can I request a makeup exam if I am sick on exam day?
answer: Yes. Submit a medical note to your instructor and the Dean of Students office within 48 hours; approved requests are rescheduled through the instructor.

question: Are calculators allowed during exams?
answer: It depends on the course policy stated on the syllabus; some quantitative courses allow a basic calculator, while others require a specific approved model or none at all.

question: How do I request extra exam time for a documented disability?
answer: Register with the Office of Accessibility Services and submit your accommodation letter to each instructor at least two weeks before the exam.

question: What happens if I miss a final exam without an approved excuse?
answer: An unexcused absence from a final exam results in a grade of zero for that exam component unless the instructor's syllabus states otherwise.

question: Can I see my exam paper after it is graded?
answer: Yes. You may request to review your graded exam during the instructor's posted office hours within two weeks of grades being released.

question: Is there a curve applied to final exam grades?
answer: Grading curves are decided per course by the instructor and, if used, are described on the syllabus; there is no university-wide curving policy.

question: How early can I arrive to prepare for the exam room?
answer: Exam rooms open 15 minutes before the scheduled start time; students arriving more than 30 minutes late may be denied entry at the proctor's discretion.

question: What identification do I need to bring to a final exam?
answer: Bring your HANU student ID card; some large lecture courses also check names against the official class roster.

question: Can I take a final exam early if I have a travel conflict?
answer: Early exams are granted only for university-sanctioned travel (athletics, research conferences) with written approval from the Dean of Students at least three weeks in advance.

question: How do I dispute a final exam grade I believe was miscalculated?
answer: Contact the instructor within one week of grade posting with the specific question you are disputing; unresolved disputes escalate to the department chair.

question: When is tuition due for the semester?
answer: Tuition payment is due two weeks before the first day of classes each semester; the exact date is posted on the Bursar's payment calendar.

question: Can I pay tuition in installments?
answer: Yes. The Bursar's Office offers a four-installment payment plan with a small enrollment fee; sign up through the Student Portal before the payment deadline.

question: What happens if I miss the tuition payment deadline?
answer: A late fee is added to your account and a registration hold is placed, which blocks course registration and transcript requests until the balance is resolved.

question: How do I apply for a need-based tuition grant?
answer: Submit the HANU Financial Aid Application along with your household income documentation through the Financial Aid portal by the priority deadline each spring.

question: Does tuition cover textbooks and course materials?
answer: No. Tuition covers instruction and standard campus fees only; textbooks, lab kits, and course materials are billed or purchased separately.

question: How do I get a refund if I withdraw from all my classes?
answer: Refunds follow a prorated schedule based on the week of withdrawal; the exact percentage table is published on the Bursar's refund policy page.

question: Is there a tuition discount for taking fewer than 12 credits?
answer: Yes. Students enrolled part time (fewer than 12 credits) are billed per credit hour instead of the flat full-time rate.

question: How do I set up a parent or sponsor to pay my tuition bill?
answer: Add an authorized payer through the Student Portal billing tab; the authorized payer receives their own login to view and pay the bill.

question: What fees are included in the mandatory campus fee?
answer: The mandatory campus fee covers the health center, campus shuttle, recreation center, and student activity funding; it is billed alongside tuition each semester.

question: Can international students pay tuition in a different currency?
answer: Payments are processed in US dollars only; the Bursar's Office lists two approved third-party services that convert foreign currency payments.

question: How do I get a tuition statement for tax or reimbursement purposes?
answer: Download the annual tuition statement from the Student Portal billing tab, or request one by visiting the Bursar's Office in person.

question: What is the penalty for a returned or failed tuition payment?
answer: A returned-payment fee is added to your account and the payment is reversed, which may re-trigger a registration hold until you submit a valid payment.

question: Where can I find my class schedule?
answer: Your current class schedule is listed under "My Schedule" on the Student Portal, including room numbers and meeting days.

question: How do I check if two of my classes overlap in time?
answer: The registration system blocks you from adding a class that overlaps an already-enrolled section, and "My Schedule" displays a weekly grid to double-check manually.

question: Can I request a schedule that avoids early morning classes?
answer: There is no guaranteed morning-free schedule, but you can filter sections by start time when browsing the course catalog before registering.

question: How do I find out which building a class meets in?
answer: Each course section lists a building and room number in the course catalog and on your "My Schedule" page; use the campus map link next to the room number.

question: What does it mean if a class is listed as TBA for room or time?
answer: TBA means the room or meeting time had not been finalized when the schedule was published; check back closer to the semester start or contact the department office.

question: Can two sections of the same course have different meeting patterns?
answer: Yes. Departments may offer one section that meets twice a week and another that meets once a week for the same course; check each section's listed pattern before registering.

question: How do I know if a class has a required lab or discussion section?
answer: Courses with a required lab or discussion list a linked section number in the catalog; you must register for both the lecture and the linked section together.

question: Does the class schedule change during university holidays?
answer: Classes do not meet on official university holidays listed in the academic calendar; instructors post makeup plans for any missed sessions if needed.

question: How far in advance is next semester's class schedule published?
answer: The tentative schedule for the next semester is published on the Registrar's site about six weeks before registration opens.

question: Can I see a professor's office hours from the class schedule page?
answer: Office hours are not shown on the schedule page; check the course syllabus or the instructor's profile on the department website.

question: What do the letters after a course number, like L or D, mean on my schedule?
answer: A trailing L marks a linked laboratory section and a trailing D marks a linked discussion section attached to the main lecture.

question: How do I get a printable version of my weekly schedule?
answer: Use the "Print Schedule" button on the "My Schedule" page to generate a PDF version of your weekly grid.

question: How do I make an appointment with academic advising?
answer: Book an appointment through the Advising tab on the Student Portal, or call the Advising Center front desk during business hours.

question: Where is the campus health center located?
answer: The Student Health Center is on the ground floor of the Wellness Building, next to the main Recreation Center entrance.

question: How do I request a letter confirming my enrollment status?
answer: Request an enrollment verification letter through the Registrar's self-service page; it is generated automatically for currently enrolled students.

question: What mental health support is available on campus?
answer: Counseling and Psychological Services offers free confidential sessions to enrolled students; book through the Wellness Building front desk or the online portal.

question: How do I report an accessibility barrier on campus?
answer: Submit a report through the Office of Accessibility Services online form, describing the location and the barrier encountered.

question: How do I get a replacement student ID card?
answer: Visit the Card Services office in the Student Union with a photo ID; a replacement fee applies unless the original card was defective.

question: Where can I find information about on-campus jobs?
answer: The Student Employment Office maintains a job board on the Student Portal listing open on-campus positions and application instructions.

question: How do I join a student club or organization?
answer: Browse active clubs on the Student Life portal and contact the club's listed officer, or attend the fall Involvement Fair to sign up in person.

question: What tutoring services are available for struggling in a course?
answer: The Academic Success Center offers free peer tutoring by subject; sign up for a session through the Tutoring tab on the Student Portal.

question: How do I request housing accommodations for a medical condition?
answer: Submit a housing accommodation request with supporting documentation to the Office of Accessibility Services before the housing selection deadline.

question: Who do I contact about a dispute with a roommate?
answer: Contact your Resident Assistant first; unresolved conflicts are escalated to the Residence Life Coordinator for mediation.

question: How do I access legal advice as a student?
answer: The Student Legal Services office offers free initial consultations for enrolled students; schedule through the Student Union front desk.

question: How do I apply to graduate?
answer: Submit the graduation application through the Student Portal by the deadline listed on the academic calendar for your intended graduation term.

question: How do I check if I have met all my degree requirements?
answer: Review your Degree Audit report on the Student Portal, which lists completed, in-progress, and remaining requirements for your major.

question: When is the commencement ceremony held?
answer: Commencement is held the weekend after final exams each spring and fall semester; the exact date is posted on the Commencement website each term.

question: Can I participate in commencement if I have one course left to finish over the summer?
answer: Yes, students within one course of completing their degree may petition to walk in commencement with approval from the Registrar.

question: How do I order my cap and gown for graduation?
answer: Order regalia through the campus bookstore's graduation portal at least four weeks before the ceremony.

question: How long does it take to receive my diploma after graduating?
answer: Diplomas are mailed approximately six to eight weeks after final grades are posted and degree conferral is confirmed.

question: What GPA do I need to graduate with honors?
answer: Latin honors cutoffs (cum laude, magna cum laude, summa cum laude) are published on the Registrar's honors policy page and are based on cumulative GPA at the time of degree conferral.

question: Can I graduate with a double major?
answer: Yes, provided you complete all requirements for both majors and file a double-major declaration with the Registrar before your final semester.

question: How do I request an official transcript after graduating?
answer: Order an official transcript through the Registrar's transcript request service; alumni pay the same per-copy fee as current students.

question: What happens if I fail to apply for graduation by the deadline?
answer: Late applications are reviewed case by case and may push your degree conferral to the following term; contact the Registrar as soon as possible.

question: Can I change my degree conferral date after applying?
answer: Yes, submit a graduation term change request through the Registrar before the original term's degree audit deadline.

question: How do I make sure my name is pronounced correctly at commencement?
answer: Submit a phonetic spelling of your name through the Commencement RSVP form so the reader can prepare it in advance.

question: How do I reset my Student Portal password?
answer: Use the "Forgot Password" link on the login page and follow the identity verification steps sent to your recovery contact on file.

question: Why can't I connect to the campus Wi-Fi network?
answer: Confirm you are using the HANU-Secure network with your Student Portal credentials; forget and rejoin the network if the connection keeps failing.

question: How do I get access to campus-licensed software?
answer: Download campus-licensed software through the IT Services software portal using your student login; some titles require connecting to the campus VPN first.

question: Who do I contact if my course website will not load?
answer: Contact the IT Help Desk through the Student Portal support ticket form, including the course name and the error message you see.

question: How do I set up my campus email on my phone?
answer: Follow the mobile setup guide on the IT Services site, which lists the mail server settings needed for common phone mail apps.

question: What do I do if I am locked out of my account after too many failed logins?
answer: Wait 15 minutes for the automatic lockout to clear, or contact the IT Help Desk to verify your identity and unlock the account immediately.

question: How do I connect to the campus VPN from off campus?
answer: Install the VPN client listed on the IT Services site and log in with your Student Portal credentials to access restricted campus resources remotely.

question: Why did my file upload fail on the course platform?
answer: Check that the file is under the platform's size limit and in an accepted format; large video files usually need to be shared as a link instead of a direct upload.

question: How do I request a laptop loan from the library?
answer: Reserve a laptop through the Library's equipment loan page; loans are first-come, first-served each semester with a maximum loan period of one week.

question: What should I do if I suspect my account was compromised?
answer: Change your password immediately and report the incident to the IT Help Desk so they can review recent login activity on your account.

question: How do I print documents from a campus computer lab?
answer: Send the print job from any lab computer to the shared print queue, then release it using your student ID card at any lab printer station.

question: Why does the course platform log me out so quickly?
answer: The platform enforces a short inactivity timeout for security; save your work frequently and consider enabling the "remember this device" option if offered.
